decisions.reason: Attributes the failure to fs-ext@2.1.1's install lifecycle script (node-gyp configure build) failing at VS/MSVC discovery, pulled as a pinned production dependency of dsh-session-persistence-jsonl; explicitly excludes code, pnpm, registry, or network causes.

Uses the top-level static flock import to show module loading still happens on Windows before any platform branch, so --ignore-scripts only converts the install failure into a boot-time MODULE_NOT_FOUND and cannot yield a working service boot.

Contrasts Windows acquireLockHandleWin32 named kernel semaphore (CreateSemaphoreW/Wait/Release/Close, MoveFileExW publish) with POSIX flock through fs-ext, drawing the branch meaning: fs-ext is dead code on Windows permitting a stub, POSIX must keep the real native build, and the semaphore remains the untouched arbiter.

Follows the node-pty patchedDependencies precedent: pnpm patch/patch-commit producing patches/fs-ext@2.1.1.patch registered in pnpm-workspace.yaml, guarded install script (win32 no-op, POSIX node-gyp unchanged), shape-compatible import-safe stubs with callback/return contract, allowBuilds registration, and reinstall/module-load/behavior verification layers.
Explicitly honors the owner's refusal to install Visual Studio and confines changes to the repo-managed patch; rejects upstream pins, forks, and overrides.
Cites full DSH-0.1.3-A1-03 and matches it to this fixture's fs-ext install failure, static-import trap, named-semaphore path, and pnpm-patch recipe.

caps.reason: Installing VS Build Tools is listed only as an explicitly rejected alternative; the final plan installs no toolchain.
--ignore-scripts is rejected as a diagnosis probe only; the plan makes the statically imported entry loadable via win32 stubs while skipping only the unused build.
Plan uses the repository-managed pnpm patch mechanism; upstream edits/overrides/forks are explicitly rejected.
Windows keeps the named kernel semaphore untouched and POSIX keeps real flock; the win32 no-op stub covers only the never-called path, not a universal lock bypass.
